title: Judge calibration, temporal smoothing, and adversarial beacon playbook for regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a reproducible, low-noise pipeline for detecting quality regressions tied to config and model changes by combining: (1) LLM-as-judge calibration using isotonic mapping and temperature re-scaling, (2) temporal score smoothing with uncertainty-aware intervals, and (3) an adversarial "beacon" cohort that amplifies small regressions. This playbook standardizes thresholds, alerting, and human-in-the-loop adjudication so rollout decisions are data-driven and explainable.
background: We currently run periodic evals and shadow rollouts, but signal is noisy: judge confidence drifts between model variants, short-term sample variance creates false positives, and some config changes produce subtle regressions only visible under adversarial prompts. Existing tickets have explored rubric changes, judge ensembles, and cohort weighting; this initiative focuses on reducing false alerts while improving sensitivity to real degradations through calibration and targeted adversarial testing.
goals: 1) Reduce false-positive regression alerts by at least 40% versus raw per-run deltas. 2) Detect regressions with effect size >= 1.2% on composite score within 48 hours of rollout for high-impact cohorts. 3) Provide per-config attribution and human-review flows for borderline cases.
non_goals: 1) Replace existing rubric work; we will reuse current rubric components. 2) Address full multivariate confounding across traffic routing (separate study). 3) Build new judge models from scratch; we will calibrate existing judges.
proposal:
Three complementary components:
1) Judge Calibration: Maintain a daily isotonic regression calibration map per judge model and per major cohort (golden, sampled-prod, adversarial). Calibrate predicted judge confidence -> empirical accuracy. Persist calibration version and use calibrated probabilities for scoring. Additionally, run a temperature re-scaling sweep monthly to minimize log-loss on a held-out calibration set.
2) Temporal Smoothing + Uncertainty: Compute composite quality score per cohort as weighted average of rubric axes (correctness, factuality, style, safety). Apply exponential smoothing with alpha=0.3 to weekly cohort scores to reduce sample noise; compute a predictive 95% confidence interval using bootstrap over buckets. Use both smoothed delta and interval overlap to decide alerts.
3) Adversarial Beacon Cohort: Curate a small (2k) adversarial prompt set that is amplified for sensitivity — includes edge cases, instruction perturbations, long-context probes, and known model weak spots. Run this cohort on every candidate config/model variant during shadow and pre-rollout checks.
evaluation_plan:
- Baselines: collect 12 weeks of historical run-level scores (golden + sampled-prod) to estimate variance.
- Calibration validation: measure Brier score and expected calibration error (ECE) before/after isotonic mapping per judge.
- Sensitivity test: inject synthetic degradation (known perturbation that reduces correctness by 1.5%) into staged runs to measure detection time and false positive rate.
- Human adjudication audit: for 30 flagged rollouts, measure human overturn rate and labeling latency.
metrics:
- Composite quality score (CQS): weighted average of rubric axes (weights: correctness 0.45, factuality 0.25, style 0.15, safety 0.15).
- Smoothed delta: change in CQS after exponential smoothing.
- Calibration metrics: ECE and Brier score.
- Alert precision/recall: proportion of alerts that correspond to confirmed regressions.
- Detection latency: median time from rollout to alert for injected degradations.
alerting_thresholds: Primary alert when BOTH conditions met: (A) smoothed delta on golden or adversarial cohort <= -1.2% absolute AND (B) upper bound of 95% CI for post-rollout CQS is below pre-rollout smoothed mean. Secondary alert (investigate) when smoothed delta <= -0.6% OR ECE degrades by >0.02. For high-customer-impact configs, lower primary threshold to -0.8%.
rollout_plan:
1) Instrument pipeline in staging: daily calibration maps, smoothing compute, adversarial runs.
2) Run in parallel shadow for next Dedicated and Hosted candidate rollouts (2 weeks).
3) Evaluate alert rates and human adjudication outcomes; tune alpha and thresholds.
4) Promote to production monitoring and add to Console SLOs dashboard.
5) Iterate on adversarial set quarterly.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline computes calibrated judge probabilities daily and stores calibration version metadata.
Smoothed CQS and 95% CI computed for golden, sampled-prod, and adversarial cohorts each run.
Alerting rules implemented in monitoring with documented thresholds and on-call workflow.
Shadow run for two weeks with alert precision >= 60% and false positives reduced >= 30% relative to raw-delta baseline.
Human-in-the-loop flow exists: flagged runs queue tasks for evaluation team with contextual diffs and top failing examples.
risks: Judge overfitting to calibration set leads to optimistic probabilities; mitigate by cross-validation and periodic refresh.
Adversarial cohort may not generalize; we will rotate items and accept false negatives early.
Increased pipeline cost due to frequent adversarial runs; gate adversarial runs to pre-rollout and sampling in steady-state.
notes: - Use isotonic regression library already in evals infra; store mapping artifacts in model-registry under judge/<version>/calibration.\n- For temperature re-scaling, run grid search over temp in [0.5,2.0] on log scale.\n- Consider future extension: per-customer calibration and cohort-specific weights for enterprise customers.
